core.title: Compose DESIRED OUTCOME statements from the template
core.given: A DESIRED OUTCOME plan artifact has a chosen direction, dimension, object of control, and an optional context clarifier.
core.when: The planner writes or revises the DESIRED OUTCOME statement.
core.then: Compose the statement exactly as `{direction} {dimension} of {object_of_control} [context_clarifier]`: the direction, then a single space, the dimension, a single space, the literal word `of`, a single space, the object of control, then — if and only if a context clarifier is set — a single space followed by the clarifier, and nothing else.
prefer: Derive the statement from the DESIRED OUTCOME's direction, dimension and object-of-control values so the text and the parts stay consistent.
Append the context clarifier after a single space only when one exists; otherwise end at the object of control.
avoid: Free-form statements that skip, reorder or rephrase the template parts (e.g. omitting the literal `of`).
Trailing spaces or placeholder text when no context clarifier is set.
core.why: A fixed composition makes every DESIRED OUTCOME statement reproducible from its direction, dimension, object of control and clarifier, so statements stay comparable and machine-checkable.
evidence: Recomputing the pattern from the DESIRED OUTCOME's direction, dimension, object_of_control and context_clarifier yields exactly the stored statement.
verification: The check recomputes the statement from the artifact's direction, dimension, object of control and context clarifier and requires an exact match with the stored statement: single-space separators, the literal word `of`, and the clarifier joined with one space only when present.
Scope: the check covers only how the statement is composed. It does not judge the content of the composing parts, and it does not cover the artifact's other fields (acceptances and the like).

In-scope artifacts are those the profile assigns to the plan-artifact role — standalone DESIRED OUTCOME definition files and DESIRED OUTCOME entries embedded in plan or product capability artifacts (roles.assignment), with the concrete DESIRED OUTCOME kind from roles.plan_artifact.kinds. The file-kind activation fact resolves to concrete artifacts through this assignment.

The change-based activation fact needs a diff-level observer that detects the statement field changed; until such an observer exists, activation relies on the operation, file-kind and task-term facts.

values: desired outcome statement field added or modified

fires: The planner writes a new DESIRED OUTCOME and must fill in its statement.
The planner rewords an existing DESIRED OUTCOME statement or changes its direction, dimension, object of control or context clarifier.
doesNotFire: A DESIRED OUTCOME's acceptances or other fields are edited without touching the statement or its composing parts.
Implementation code or tests are written that do not author DESIRED OUTCOME statements.

profileRequirements.meaning: The concrete plan-artifact kinds that carry DESIRED OUTCOME statements, so the rule's activation and its check know which artifacts are in scope.

How artifacts are assigned to the plan-artifact role, so the file-kind activation fact and the check resolve which containers are in scope: standalone DESIRED OUTCOME definition files plus DESIRED OUTCOME entries embedded in plan or product capability artifacts are plan-artifact role members.

bunOnly.reason: The template-literal-with-ternary rendering is this stack's concrete encoding of the pattern; the core states the same composition in stack-neutral prose.

bunOnly.text: Term `statement_pattern` (the DESIRED OUTCOME statement composition): `${direction} ${dimension} of ${object_of_control}${context_clarifier ? ' ' + context_clarifier : ''}` — clarifier is optional and, when present, joined with one space.
bunOnly.reason: The term id `statement_pattern` and the template-literal encoding are realization details of this stack's checker; the core states the obligation in `then` and describes the recompute-and-compare check generically in `verification`.

neutralityNotes: The obligation itself is stack-neutral: it composes one string from the DESIRED OUTCOME's own fields, so the core keeps the ATDD plan-artifact vocabulary (DESIRED OUTCOME, direction, dimension, object of control, context clarifier, planner) — these belong to the ATDD planning schema, not to any stack. The profile supplies what is concrete: which artifact kinds play the plan-artifact role (roles.plan_artifact.kinds = desired outcome) and how artifacts are assigned to it (roles.assignment = 'DESIRED OUTCOME definition files / DESIRED OUTCOME entries in plan or product capability artifacts.'), which the file-kind activation fact and the check resolve through, per revision 2 feedback. No concrete paths are given in the authoritative rewrite, so no layout path keys are claimed. What could not be made neutral: the JavaScript template-literal/ternary rendering in `then` and in `verifier_detail[0]`, plus the term id `statement_pattern` — realization encodings of the same pattern, kept as bunOnly. Activation fires/doesNotFire were carried into the core (with 'coder-side code' generalized to 'implementation code or tests'); they are not item ids under the numbering scheme and so have no classification entries. No severity or disposition is declared in bun.json, so core.verification records only the check, its scope, the profile-resolved artifact scope, and the observer gap.
